item.title: Wakefit Q2: Profit Remains Flat YoY At ₹16 Cr, Revenue Crosses ₹450 Cr
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: Listed mattress brand Wakefit reported a net profit of ₹15.9 Cr in second quarter (Q1) of the fiscal year 2026-27…
item.content:encoded:
Listed mattress brand Wakefit reported a net profit of ₹15.9 Cr in second quarter (Q1) of the fiscal year 2026-27 (FY27), almost flat from nearly ₹16 Cr in the year-ago quarter. However, on a quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) basis, the bottom line tanked 32% from ₹23.4 Cr in Q1 FY27.

The company attributed the sequential decline in profitability to rising commodity prices, geopolitical disruptions and the “challenging” operating environment.

“The operating environment remained challenging during the quarter, with crude-linked raw materials, particularly Polyol and TDI, continuing to remain elevated, with further price increases witnessed in recent months. Geopolitical disruptions in West Asia also impacted raw material availability and logistics across the industry…,” said Wakefit cofounder and executive director Chaitanya Ramalingegowda.

Despite this, operating revenue rose nearly 20% to a record ₹452 Cr in the quarter under review as against ₹376.9 Cr in Q2 FY26. Sequentially, the top line also rose 11.6% from ₹404.9 Cr in the preceding quarter.

While mattresses brought in 66% of revenue, furniture, furnishings and decor contributed the remaining 38%. 

Including other income of ₹16 Cr, Wakefit’s total income stood at ₹468 Cr in Q2 FY27. 

Meanwhile, total expenses for the quarter under review also shot up 19% to ₹441.4 Cr compared to ₹370.5 Cr in Q2 FY26. The listed company also incurred additional tax expenses of ₹10.7 Cr during the quarter.

“The company recorded a deferred tax charge of ₹6.4 Cr in Q2 FY27, compared with nil in Q2 FY26 and ₹7.3 Cr in Q1 FY27. This is attributable to two factors: (i) normal-course reversal of timing differences relating to depreciation and provisions as they unwind through the P&L, and (ii) the unwinding of the deferred tax asset on carried-forward losses,” said the company in a statement.

In its investor presentation, the company said that its operating EBITDA rose 25.8% to ₹30.5 Cr in the quarter under review compared to ₹24.2 Cr in Q2 FY26. Operating EBITDA margin also improved to 6.7% from 6.4% in the year-ago quarter.

On the operational front, Wakefit opened 41 new offline stores in Q2 FY27, taking its total company-owned store count to 205 across 137 cities. It also had a presence across 2,589 multi-brand outlets spanning 787 towns and cities.

Wakefit said that its own channels contributed 70% of its sales in Q2 FY27, while external channels accounted for the remaining 30%.

The company also noted it operated a 1.6 Lakh sq. ft. mother warehouse in Hosur, 10 inventory holding points and 26 points of delivery at the end of September 2026.

“Our planned FY27 capex of around ₹100 Cr to ₹120 Cr remains on track, with nearly 80% allocated towards retail expansion, particularly our jumbo store format. Construction of our first jumbo store in Bengaluru is progressing, and we are targeting its launch in Q2 FY28,” added Ramalingegowda.

Shares of Wakefit closed Thursday’s trading session 1.1% lower at ₹138.75 on the BSE.

item.title: NHRC Member Flags Meta-UNICEF Funding Ties Amid CSAM Scrutiny
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Social media giant Meta has once again come under the radar of Indian authorities over alleged child sexual abuse material…
item.content:encoded:
Social media giant Meta has once again come under the radar of Indian authorities over alleged child sexual abuse material (CSAM) prevalent on Meta-owned platforms.

Now, National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) member Priyank Kanoon has urged the women and child developement (WCD) ministry to look into the financial relationship between the social media giant and the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF).

Citing advocacy group Legal Rights Observatory, Kanoongo reportedly said that UNICEF is trying to offer its help to Indian authorities in the ongoing government probe into the child sexual abuse material (CSAM), sold as ads, on Meta platforms. 

Speaking with news agency PTI, Kanoongo flagged that Meta has given ‘millions of dollars” to UNICEF and continues to fund the organisation. He argued that this financial relationship could create a conflict of interest, particularly because UNICEF is engaged in child-protection work while Meta faces allegations involving exploitative content on its platforms.

In a letter written to WCD secretary Anil Malik, he called for a probe into the financial ties between Meta and UNICEF. Kanoongo also raised concerns that UNICEF could end up serving Meta’s interests rather than supporting child protection. He also urged the government to ensure that Meta is not allowed to use UNICEF as a “shield to evade accountability”.

“Therefore, there is a concern that this organisation, which is supposed to work on the issue of child sexual exploitation material while receiving funding from Meta, might end up serving Meta’s interests. The activist group has expressed apprehension that this organisation could potentially work in favour of Meta’s interests,” Kanoongo reportedly said.

The NHRC member said that he has already brought the matter to the attention of the WCD ministry, external affairs ministry, home affairs ministry and the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre.

He also urged Indian authorities to keep the alleged conflict of interest in mind while conducting investigations and taking enforcement action. The concern, he claimed, was that allegations of vested interests being served through financial funding should not turn out to be true.

This comes a months after a BBC Eye documentary, aired in July, allegedly found that Instagram was running paid adverts promoting CSAM in India. As per Kanoongo, the NHRC has already identified about 100 such instances.

The aftermath saw the Centre pull up the social media giant and summon the company’s top leadership. The government also directed Meta to strengthen CSAM detection, increase human oversight of moderation and improve safeguards for content in Indian languages and local contexts.

Earlier reports suggested that government was considering waving off Meta’s “safe harbour” protection under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act, 2000. This could have potentially forced the company to face greater legal liability in cases of CSAM or other illegal content being posted on Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. 

Post this, the social media giant agreed to report instances of child sexual abuse to the local law enforcement agencies in September. Days later, Meta also said that it has introduced LLM-driven systems to identify “signposting” within ads to counter predators who advertise illicit material in ways that can evade automated detection. 

The social media juggernaut also claims to have deployed AI-driven sweeps to uncover missed CSAM material and integrated “red-teaming” AI agents to strengthen detection mechanisms.

item.title: Yatra Slips Into The Red In Q2, Reports ₹78 Lakh Loss
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: Online travel aggregator (OTA) Yatra swung to the red and reported a consolidated net loss of ₹78.4 Lakhs in the…
item.content:encoded:
Online travel aggregator (OTA) Yatra swung to the red and reported a consolidated net loss of ₹78.4 Lakhs in the second quarter (Q2) of the fiscal year 2026-27 (FY27). In contrast, the travel tech platform has reported a net profit of ₹14.3 Cr in Q2 FY26 and ₹33.9 Lakhs in Q1 FY27.

The losses came despite the company raking in ₹1.7 Cr in one-time deferred tax benefits during the quarter.

The bottom line was primarily impacted as the company’s revenue from operations tanked 39.1% to ₹213.6 Cr in the quarter under review from ₹350.9 Cr in Q2 FY26. However, on a sequential basis, Yatra’s top line rose 13.7% from ₹187.9 Cr in the preceding quarter.

The OTA attributed the losses to the “challenging operating environment”, lower MICE (meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions) volumes, and the reorientation of the MICE vertical towards smaller corporate group programmes.

“… Our year-on-year profitability was impacted primarily by MICE, which faced an exceptionally strong comparable quarter last year and a tactical shift towards smaller corporate group programmes amid prevailing uncertainty…,” said Yatra CEO Siddhartha Gupta.

Including other income of ₹4.4 Cr, Yatra’s total income stood at ₹218 Cr in Q2 FY27. 

Meanwhile, total expenses for the quarter under review declined 35% to ₹219.9 Cr compared to ₹339 Cr in Q2 FY26. The company also incurred an additional tax expense of ₹59.3 Lakh during the quarter.

Revenue less service cost (RLSC), which is essentially the gross margin, declined 0.2% to ₹125.5 Cr in Q2 FY27. As a result, EBITDA declined 47% YoY to ₹13.2 Cr, while EBITDA margin stood at 10.48%during the quarter under review.

In a statement, the company’s gross bookings grew 6% YoY and 3% QoQ to ₹2,165.5 Cr in Q2 FY27. During the quarter, Yatra said that it added 54 new corporate customers with an estimated annual revenue potential of ₹203.5 Cr. 

“We continue to make progress on our strategic priorities, including expanding into the SME and mid-market segments through Travel Pro, strengthening our expense management offering through RECAP, expanding hotel supply and leveraging AI-led automation. These initiatives are helping us broaden our addressable market and build a more scalable business, positioning us for sustainable growth and improved profitability over the medium term,” added Gupta.

Yatra’s US Entity On Nasdaq’s Radar

Separately, the travel tech platform’s US-listed entity, Yatra Online Inc, said that it has received a letter from Nasdaq after its shares traded below the exchange’s minimum $1 closing bid price for more than a month. This has effectively put the travel tech company on a compliance watch. 

The company said that the notice does not immediately delist the company’s shares from the Nasdaq Capital Market. However, the OTA said that it has been given a timeline of 180 days, until May 10, 2027, to regain compliance. To do so, its shares must close at $1 or higher for at least 10 consecutive business days, even though Nasdaq may require up to 20 consecutive days in certain cases.

If Yatra fails to meet the requirement by May next year, it may qualify for an additional 180-day compliance period. This would require the company to meet Nasdaq’s other continued-listing thresholds and formally notify the exchange of its intention to cure the deficiency.

A reverse stock split is among the options available to lift the share price. Yatra said it may consider such a move if necessary, but cautioned that there is no assurance it will regain compliance. Nevertheless, Yatra said it intends to closely monitor its closing bid price and may evaluate available options to restore compliance. 

The notice highlights the pressure facing the travel-tech company’s US-listed shares. As of 1:13 AM IST, shares of Yatra Online Inc were trading at $0.77, down 18% in the past six months and nearly 57% lower on a year-to-date (YTD) basis.

This comes as the US-listed Yatra Online Inc has been reporting increased net losses, compressed margins and falling revenues. Slowing growth in core verticals, market volatility and rising short-term trade-related borrowings have further led to the sell-off in the stock.

But a sustained share price below $1 can further reduce liquidity, deter institutional investors and complicate future fundraising.

Meanwhile, shares of India-listed Yatra closed Thursday’s trading session 0.94% lower at ₹81.03 on the BSE.

item.title: Exclusive: Fireside Ventures Sees Another Key Exit, Days After Cofounder Vinay Singh
item.dc:creator: Bismah Malik
item.description: Consumer tech focussed venture capital firm Fireside Ventures has seen a second exit from its leadership and investment team in…
item.content:encoded:
Consumer tech focussed venture capital firm Fireside Ventures has seen a second exit from its leadership and investment team in two weeks. 

Prayag Mohanty, principal at Fireside Ventures, who led its early-stage bets, has quit the firm, Inc42 has learnt from multiple sources.  

His exit follows a bigger leadership change at Fireside Ventures. Earlier this month, the firm said that cofounder and partner Vinay Singh has stepped down after nearly a decade at the firm.

Responding to Inc42’s query, Fireside Ventures confirmed Mohanty’s exit. “Prayag Mohanty is moving on from his role of Principal at Fireside Ventures. We value his contributions made during his time with us, and wish him the best in his future endeavours,” Fireside said in a statement to Inc42.

Another Blow For Fireside 

Mohanty joined Fireside Ventures as a Principal in January 2020. He was one of five principals listed on the firm’s investment team, alongside Ankur Khaitan, Shuchi Pandya, Varun Varma and Ankita Balotia. 

As a principal leading Fireside’s early stage investments, Mohanty fronted several of the firm’s seed stage bets over the past year, including a ₹8 Cr round in Gurugram-based men’s personal care brand Unbound, a ₹20 Cr round in Noida-based Oroos Confectionery and another ₹8 Cr seed round in kids wellness startup Wellopia.

In earlier media reports, he was quoted as saying that Fireside Ventures is ramping up investments in pre-product-market-fit and even pre-revenue startups through a co-investment model with other funds and angel investors, with 8-10 such deals in the pipeline from the new third fund.

Before Fireside, Mohanty had spent about seven years as a principal at IvyCap Ventures from 2013 to 2020, and was involved in deals for listed jewellery giant BlueStone, BiryaniByKilo and Vinculum. 

The key departures come less than a year after Fireside announced the final close of its Fund IV at ₹2,265 Cr (about $253 Mn) in December 2025. With Singh’s exit, the firm is being led by founder and managing partner Kanwaljit Singh and cofounders and partners Kannan Sitaram and Dipanjan Basu.

The fund drew commitments from LPs including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA), Investment Corporation of Dubai, HarbourVest, Waterfield and Fidelity International. With Fund IV, Fireside’s assets under management across four funds stand at ₹5,300 Cr (about $650 Mn).

item.title: Exclusive: Why Zupee’s AI Pivot Was A Smokescreen For Its Shutdown
item.dc:creator: Debarghya Sil
item.description: Delhi NCR-based gaming startup Zupee has nothing more to lose. For one, it has laid off its entire workforce. Then,…
item.content:encoded:
Delhi NCR-based gaming startup Zupee has nothing more to lose. For one, it has laid off its entire workforce. Then, its announcement of a pivot towards AI has failed to see the light of day. 

According to sources, the startup has provided severance pay to the affected employees, covering the period until January 2027, and its October pivot was a veiled attempt to present the impending closure. 

The final round of layoffs coincided with Zupee’s public announcement of its foray into AI, Inc42 has learnt. On October 16, the startup said it was positioning its existing technological capabilities as the foundation for its AI ambitions. However, it did not disclose its new gig.

Further, the October layoffs followed two earlier rounds of job cuts. Zupee sacked around 200 employees 10 months before its October layoff and nearly 170 employees before that. At its peak, the startup employed close to 500 employees.  

Inc42 reached out to Zupee for comment but did not receive a response.

Zupee Disguises Shutdown?

On October 16, Zupee announced that it was exiting the gaming business and would focus on building AI-led ventures. The ailing startup said it would leverage its experience of serving over 200 Mn users to develop AI products for Indian consumers.

“There was no AI plan. It was a damage control exercise to hide the fact that Zupee was winding down its operations. Currently, they have no employees left, barring 3-4 who are working with the founders,” sources told Inc42.

Meanwhile, Zupee has also shut down its astrology platform, NeoAstro, and its microdrama venture, Zupee Studio, as part of its restructuring in October. The closure of these businesses suggest that Zupee may have already been winding down.

Zupee entered the microdrama segment as part of this diversification strategy. It was in advanced discussions to acquire Vertical TV. “However, the proposed acquisition eventually fell through,” sources said. Inc42 could not independently ascertain the reasons behind this.

What Happens To Zupee’s $120 Mn Warchest?

Founded in 2018 by Dilsher Singh Malhi and Siddhant Saurabh, Zupee built its business around mobile versions of traditional Indian games, including Ludo, Snakes and Ladders and Carrom.

Over the years, it had raised over $120 Mn from investors, including Z47, Orios Venture Partners, Nepean Capital, WestCap Group, Tomales Bay Capital and AJ Capital.

With its gaming business discontinued and its other consumer ventures reportedly shut down, questions remain about the startup’s remaining cash reserves, assets and outstanding liabilities.

Inc42 reached out to Zupee’s investors, including Z47 Partners and Nepean Capital, to understand whether they were informed about the impending shutdown and workforce reduction, and whether the AI pivot was presented to them as a genuine business strategy. 

Investors have also been asked about the current status of their investment, the possibility of recovering unutilised capital and whether the management has initiated discussions around a potential shutdown or liquidation. However, none of the investors responded to Inc42’s queries.

For a startup that raised close to $120 Mn and built a consumer platform with a claimed user base of over 200 Mn, the developments mark a significant reversal from its earlier growth ambitions.

item.title: NPCI Unveils New MDR-Funded Scheme To Promote UPI Among Small Merchants
item.dc:creator: Akshit Pushkarna
item.description: The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has introduced a new scheme to expand UPI acceptance among small merchants. Under…
item.content:encoded:
The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has introduced a new scheme to expand UPI acceptance among small merchants. Under the new initiative, the payments body will offer incentives to banks for deploying QR codes and soundboxes to further drive transaction growth. 

The scheme will be funded through a portion of the merchant discount rate (MDR) earned by banks and other UPI ecosystem participants.

In a circular dated November 11, NPCI announced the launch of the ‘UPI Vyapaar Saksham Scheme’, which aims to address the limited availability of digital payment acceptance infrastructure among small merchants, particularly in smaller cities and towns.

The scheme will run for a period of three years from the implementation of UPI MDR, which is yet to be notified. 

The initiative will focus on merchants in Tier III to Tier VI cities, northeastern states, Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh. Small merchants covered under notified central government schemes, including PM SVANidhi and PM Vishwakarma, will also be eligible.

NPCI defines small merchants as businesses with an annual turnover of up to ₹40 Lakh in the preceding financial year.

The fund will be created from MDR collections rather than a separate government allocation. Each issuing bank, acquiring bank, payer payment service provider (PSP) and UPI application provider participating in UPI will contribute 5% of its MDR share to the fund. 

The contribution will exclude MDR earned from categories that are not eligible for the scheme. 

The fund will be divided into three components, with the largest allocation going towards increasing transaction volumes among existing merchants.

Under the first component, which accounts for 30% of the fund, acquiring banks will receive ₹300 for every physical QR code and ₹750 for every soundbox deployed at an eligible new small merchant. To qualify, a merchant will have to record at least 25 eligible transactions in any two months of a quarter, with a minimum transaction value of ₹5,000 per month.

For context, the scheme defines eligible transactions as successfully settled UPI payments of up to ₹2,000 at small merchants. It excludes transactions that are subsequently reversed, refunded or cancelled, as well as artificial transactions created by splitting payments to remain below the ₹2,000 threshold.

The second component will receive 50% of the fund and reward acquiring banks for growing UPI transaction volumes among existing and newly onboarded small merchants. 

Banks will need to demonstrate at least 5% QoQ growth in eligible transaction volumes to qualify for incentives. They will receive 0.03% of the aggregate value of eligible transactions, with merchants in the targeted geographies receiving an additional 50% incentive.

The remaining 20% will be allocated towards incremental growth in targeted geographies. Under this component, acquiring banks will receive an incentive of 0.2% of the incremental value of eligible transactions compared with the previous quarter, over and above the incentive under the second component.

NPCI has also set out ambitious deployment targets. The scheme is expected to facilitate 6 Lakh to 1 Cr new physical QR code deployments and 5 Lakh to 10 Lakh new soundbox installations annually. It also aims to drive 30% to 50% annual growth in transaction volumes among existing small merchants.

UPI’s MDR Transition

This comes as the Centre is all set to re-introduce MDR on select “high-value” UPI transactions after nearly six years of a zero-MDR regime.

In September 2026, the government notified amendments to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, paving the way for MDR on select merchant transactions. Subsequently, NPCI introduced a framework under which person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above ₹2,000 would attract an MDR of 0.4%, capped at ₹300 for transactions of ₹75,000 and above.

Transactions of up to ₹2,000 and peer-to-peer (P2P) payments have been kept outside the MDR framework. Small merchants receiving up to ₹1 Lakh per month through UPI QR codes under the P2M-to-P2P merchant (P2PM) category were also exempted from MDR.

The government said the move was intended to create a sustainable revenue stream for banks and payment companies while supporting the infrastructure required to operate UPI at scale. The MDR collected is distributed among ecosystem participants rather than retained by the government. 

The proposed MDR framework  faced pushback from retailers, with a possible deferment of its rollout to January next year. Later, the imposition was pushed beyond Diwali. Four days after Diwali, NPCI is yet to come out with a date for the implementation for this. 

Whenever MDR comes into place, the new NPCI scheme would effectively channel a portion of the MDR revenue back into expanding UPI acceptance among this merchant segment.

That said, NPCI will administer the fund, validate incentive claims and oversee settlements. Acquiring banks will submit claims quarterly, with NPCI required to process incentive payments within 30 days of claim submission, subject to validation.

The scheme also mandates that acquiring banks report merchant locations, unique merchant identifiers and details of deployed QR codes and soundboxes to enable transaction-level monitoring.

The underlying policy shift is significant: while the MDR framework creates a revenue stream for UPI ecosystem participants, the new scheme attempts to use a portion of that revenue to address the infrastructure gap that has kept digital payment acceptance concentrated among larger merchants and in urban markets.

item.title: Jensen Huang Resigns As CEO Of Chipmaker NVIDIA
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: Jensen Huang has resigned as the chief executive officer (CEO) of chipmaker NVIDIA. This brings the curtains down on Huang’s…
item.content:encoded:
Jensen Huang has resigned as the chief executive officer (CEO) of chipmaker NVIDIA. This brings the curtains down on Huang’s 33-year old tenure as the head of the company, which he cofounded in 1993. 

In a statement, the company’s board said that Huang had stepped down as president, CEO and board member with immediate effect.

This development follows revelations that he had two extramarital affairs, one of which involved a woman accused of spying for China.

Meanwhile, chief financial officer (CFO) Colette Kress will take over as the interim CEO of the company. She will retain her role as the head of finance. The board will now reportedly consider both internal and external candidates to appoint a new successor to Huang.

In its press statement, the chipmaker also announced the appointment of former Synopsys CEO Harvey Jones as the “first-ever” chair of the company’s board.

“… I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years… We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders,” said Kress in a statement.

Born in Taiwan in 1963, Jensen Huang and his family moved to the US at the age of five. In the 1990s, he joined hands with two engineers from Sun Microsystems, Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, to set up NVIDIA, a startup that would initially sell graphics hardware.

The game-changing moment came in 2012 when a team of computer scientists used two NVIDIA graphics cards to train AlexNet, a system that learned to recognise objects in images. In 2016, Huang personally delivered the company’s first DGX-1 AI computing system to OpenAI. Five years later, NVIDIA was making $215.9 Bn in annual revenue.

NVIDIA has since become integral to the development and operation of AI systems such as ChatGPT. But how did Huang go from being the belle of the AI ball to being ousted from a company he cofounded?

How Jensen Huang Was Undone

The development comes nearly a month after New York Times reported that US intelligence agencies had uncovered a romantic interest between Jensen and Singapore-based AI infrastructure company Megaspeed’s executive Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy who fed information back to Beijing. 

Megaspeed is said to have purchased $4.8 Bn in NVIDIA chips over the last two years. The company has previously reportedly been probed by both the US and Singaporean officials over suspicions that the firm was illegally supplying chips to China. 

In a letter written to NVIDIA employees, the outgoing CEO apologised for the affair and confirmed that he had cheated on his wife.

The matter took a sudden turn yesterday after the New York Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare. Afterwards, Reuters also reported that Jensen Huang had another extramarital affair with a second NVIDIA employee.

Before the allegations of the third affair came to light, the company’s board met on Thursday (IST) and voted to oust Jensen Huang. 

Meanwhile, NVIDIA has ordered an internal probe into the matter, while US President Donald Trump separately reportedly confirmed that the FBI was also investigating the case.

The ripples are also being felt back home. As NVIDIA’s influence extends beyond GPU supply to financing and strategic partnerships, Indian players are facing questions around debt exposure, customer commitments, GPU depreciation and whether their infrastructure investments can withstand a global market correction.

item.title: PlayBlue Taps KL Rahul As Investor, Eyes 100-Store Sports Retail Network
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Sports retail startup PlayBlue has onboarded cricketer KL Rahul as an investor and brand ambassador days ahead of launching its…
item.content:encoded:
Sports retail startup PlayBlue has onboarded cricketer KL Rahul as an investor and brand ambassador days ahead of launching its flagship store in Bengaluru. PlayBlue is set to open a 20,000 sq ft flagship store on 80 Feet Road in Bengaluru and launch its mobile app this Saturday (November 14).

The flagship store will be spread across three retail floors, a café level and a rooftop terrace. Its product portfolio will span sports apparel, footwear, equipment, accessories, recovery products and sports nutrition, catering to both amateur and professional athletes.

Beyond conventional retail, PlayBlue is positioning itself around specialised product discovery and in-store experiences. The store will offer gait analysis, treadmill-based footwear testing and cricket bat sensors to help customers assess products before making purchases.

It will also provide services such as racquet stringing, cricket bat knocking and bicycle servicing.

The rooftop space, called The Playground, will have a pickleball court, one-on-one futsal turf and a cricket net equipped with a bowling machine. The company also plans to host community classes, recovery sessions and sports club events at the venue.

The startup aims to expand to over 100 stores across 25 Indian cities over the next five years.

Founded in 2025 by former GMR Sports’ CEO Satyam Trivedi and former Cult.fit’s executive Jayam Vora, PlayBlue sells an assortment of athleisure, footwear, gear, fitness equipment, recovery products and nutrition through its retail stores and ecommerce platform.

“We’re building the store we wanted to walk into ourselves. Having KL Rahul on board as both an investor and our ambassador gives us a partner who knows what the right gear means to someone who plays,” Vora said.

The development comes months after PlayBlue secured $2.7 Mn (₹25.7 Cr) in a seed funding round in July, co-led by Centre Court Capital and MIXI Global, with participation from WEH Ventures.

To note, KL Rahul has backed numerous brands in the Indian startup ecosystem, including Boldfit, Flam, XYXX and Metaman.

With the Indian sports market projected to more than double to $130 Bn by FY30, investors’ interest remains lukewarm in backing startups in this space.

For instance, fitness and sportswear brand Boldfit raised around ₹400 Cr (about $41.8 Mn) from Bharat Value Fund as part of its Series B funding round in October, for its nationwide retail expansion, product innovation, and manufacturing. 

Earlier in April, sportstech startup SportVot raised ₹32.7 Cr (about $3.8 Mn) in a fresh funding round led by IAN Alpha Fund, to expand its international presence and strengthen its AI-powered production and analytics capabilities.

item.title: Turtlemint Trims Q2 Loss By 67% YoY To ₹26 Cr, Revenue Surges 35%
item.dc:creator: Akshit Pushkarna
item.description: Insurtech company Turtlemint managed to cut its consolidated net loss for the September quarter (Q2 FY27) by 67% to ₹25.8…
item.content:encoded:
Insurtech company Turtlemint managed to cut its consolidated net loss for the September quarter (Q2 FY27) by 67% to ₹25.8 Cr from ₹78.5 Cr in the year-ago period. On a sequential basis, the company’s loss declined 32% from ₹37.8 Cr. 

Operating revenue for the quarter surged 35% YoY and 16% QoQ to ₹342.2 Cr. Including other income of ₹9.5 Cr, total income for the quarter surged to ₹351.7 Cr. 

Meanwhile, total expenses for the quarter also zoomed by 25% to ₹375.2 Cr in the quarter under review from ₹299.8 Cr in Q2 FY26. The company also incurred an additional tax expense of ₹2.3 Cr in Q2 FY27. 

In its investor presentation, Turtlemint said that its EBITDA loss stood at ₹17 Cr in Q2 FY27, which the management called the lowest ever during the quarterly earnings call. In contrast, the company reported an EBITDA loss of ₹40 Cr in Q2 FY26. 

“Q2 FY27 has been another quarter of consistent delivery. Platform premium grew 55% You and revenue from operations rose 35%, underlining the depth of the distribution network we have built over the years. Our service EBITDA grew 47% YoY this quarter,which shows that every incremental Rupee of business is becoming more efficient to serve,” said Turtlemint cofounder and CEO Dhirendra Mahyavanshi and cofounder and COO Anand Prabhudesai in a joint statement.

On the operational front, Turtlemint noted that it processed platform premiums worth ₹1,214 Cr in the quarter under review, up 55% YoY. For context, platform premiums refers to the total value of insurance premiums on policies sold through Turtlemint’s platform during the period. 

The company also claims to have added 37,000 new digital partners in the quarter under review, taking its total quarterly active digital partner base to 93,000.

Responding to a question about the impact of IRDAI’s new insurance reforms, the management, during the earnings call, estimated that the income of point-of-sales-persons (POSPs) could fall by about ₹1,000 a month compared to its agents. The company believes that this decline could be offset by selling one or two additional policies. 

The management, however, declined to share FY28 stress-case numbers, saying it will do so once the final IRDAI rules are out. But it expects service EBITDA to hold flat in absolute terms next year.

Founded in 2015 by Prabhudesai and Mahyavanshi, Turtlemint operates an insurance distribution platform, connecting consumers with insurers through a network of financial advisors for car, bike, health, and term life insurance.

Operationally, the company claims to be active in 19,186 pincodes with 83 physical branches.

Shares of Turtlemint closed 1.5% higher at ₹61.38 apiece on the BSE today.

item.title: OpenAI Brings API Inference Residency To India To Deepen Enterprise AI Adoption
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: ChatGPT maker OpenAI has introduced local inference and data processing for its APIs in India, adding to its efforts to…
item.content:encoded:
ChatGPT maker OpenAI has introduced local inference and data processing for its APIs in India, adding to its efforts to expand the commercialisation of ChatGPT in its largest market.

For context, local data inferencing allows businesses to ensure that both API requests and the computing required to generate responses take place within India for supported workloads. It is initially available for the GPT-6 Luna model and extends OpenAI’s existing data residency options in the country.

OpenAI’s India enterprise head Nitin Bawankule pointed out that local inference gives businesses greater control over where their data is processed and could help more organisations move from experimenting with AI to deploying it in their day-to-day operations.

“Some Indian businesses have not fully deployed AI for important work because they need the information involved to be processed within the country,” Bawankule said.

To use the new offering, customers need to create a new API project, select India as the location for both data storage and processing, and use the corresponding India regional endpoint.

With the launch, India joins Australia and Japan as the latest markets where OpenAI has introduced API inference residency.

Global AI Giants Push For Data Localisation In India

Data localisation has emerged as an important consideration in enterprise AI adoption. While global AI models offer advanced capabilities, businesses handling sensitive information require a greater understanding of where their data is going.

Storage and processing of data before model deployment is something that cannot be compromised from a security perspective for banks, financial institutions and government agencies. For these clients, data residency and infrastructure requirements can limit the use of international frontier AI models in production environments.

OpenAI is not the first international AI company looking to address India’s data localisation requirements.

In August, Anthropic announced plans to bring in-country inference for its Claude AI models to India through Amazon Bedrock, AWS’ managed service for building generative AI applications. The move was aimed at addressing data residency and infrastructure requirements that have kept banks, financial institutions and government agencies from deploying international AI models in production.

Anthropic has since made similar data residency capabilities available for certain models on AWS Bedrock.

For Indian AI startups such as Sarvam AI, locally hosted inference has also been an important differentiator when competing with global AI players. However, the entry of OpenAI and Anthropic into this segment could narrow that advantage as international companies begin offering similar capabilities in the country.

For OpenAI, data inferencing is another piece of its India revenue. The AI giant has established a strong hold on the Indian market, where more than 10 Cr people interact with ChatGPT on a weekly basis. The company is looking to monetise its India holding.

OpenAI Expands Its Business Offering On ChatGPT

In a bid to deepen its engagement with businesses, OpenAI introduced Businesses in ChatGPT, a beta offering that allows businesses to claim and manage their profiles through a new Business Hub. Companies can update their information, add product feeds and access aggregated insights into how users discover and engage with them on ChatGPT.

These insights include business mentions, website clicks and discovery topics across conversations where their websites are cited.

OpenAI has also introduced Business Agents, which allow customers to interact with businesses, explore their offerings and ask product-related questions directly within ChatGPT. However, the feature is initially available only to eligible ecommerce and online service businesses in the US.

Businesses in markets where ChatGPT is available, including India, can claim their profiles through Business Hub, subject to eligibility and verification requirements.

OpenAI’s broader efforts to expand its presence in India include investments and partnerships to develop domestic AI infrastructure.

Earlier this year, the company partnered with Tata Group to develop domestic AI data centre capacity. It has also extended data residency capabilities for certain models through AWS Bedrock.

item.title: Exclusive: Sofina To Lead PlatinumRx’s $32 Mn Funding At $200 Mn Valuation
item.dc:creator: Debarghya Sil
item.description: Online pharmacy startup PlatinumRx is in talks to raise around $32 Mn (over ₹300 Cr) in a funding round led…
item.content:encoded:
Online pharmacy startup PlatinumRx is in talks to raise around $32 Mn (over ₹300 Cr) in a funding round led by Belgium-based investment giant Sofina Ventures, as per sources familiar with the discussion. The proposed transaction is expected to value the Bengaluru-based startup somewhere in the range of $150-200 Mn (₹1,400-1,878 Cr). 

The proposed investment comes around a year after the startup raised $6 Mn in its Series A round. Stellaris Venture Partners and India Quotient backed the startup in its Series A round. The startup had previously raised around $800K in a seed round in April 2024, also led by India Quotient.

Inc42 has reached out to the aforementioned investors to understand whether they will participate in the round. 

The September 2025 round had helped the startup strengthen its supply chain, expand fulfilment capabilities and build its product and technology teams. It had also outlined plans to add five fulfilment centres and improve sourcing efficiencies to make affordable substitute medicines more accessible.

The discussions are understood to be ongoing, and the final terms of the transaction, including the valuation and investor participation, could change. Questions sent to PlatinumRx and Sofina Ventures didn’t elicit any response at the time of publishing the story.

If concluded, the funding round would mark a significant jump in PlatinumRx’s valuation and provide it with the fresh capital required to strengthen its presence in India’s online pharmacy market. 

Founded in 2023 by Ashutosh Pandey and Piyush Kumar, PlatinumRx operates an online pharmacy platform focused on helping consumers find affordable alternatives to prescribed medicines. 

The platform recommends substitute medicines with the same composition, allowing customers to access lower-cost options, particularly for recurring and chronic medication requirements. These medicines are sourced directly from pharmaceutical companies and offer alternatives with the same composition, addressing the price difference between branded medicines and their substitutes.

It claims to have served over 10 Lakh customers till date.

The proposed funding comes amid continued investor interest in specialised healthcare and pharmacy platforms. While quick commerce platforms are expanding into medicine delivery, online pharmacy startups are also attempting to build differentiated models around affordability, assortment and access.

Broadly, the online pharmacy segment has continued to attract sizable investments. Quick medicine delivery startup Plazza raised $15 Mn in a Series A funding round in July 2026, co-led by Accel, Elevation Capital and Nexus Venture Partners, with participation from existing investors All In Capital and Better Capital. 

The Bengaluru-based startup operates a pharmacy-first quick commerce model focused on 15-30 minute medicine deliveries. On the other hand, last year, Truemeds had raised $85 Mn in funding to scale generic medicine delivery.

item.title: Ola Electric Q2 Loss Down 13% To ₹362 Cr, Revenue Dips 39%
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Ola Electric narrowed its consolidated net loss by 13% Yo) to ₹362 Cr in the September quarter (Q2 FY27) from…
item.content:encoded:
Ola Electric narrowed its consolidated net loss by 13% Yo) to ₹362 Cr in the September quarter (Q2 FY27) from ₹418 Cr in the same quarter last year. However, the E2W maker’s top line continued to face pressure on its top line, with operating revenue declining 39% YoY to ₹421 Cr from ₹690 Cr.

On a sequential basis, the company’s loss widened 8% from ₹336 Cr in Q1 FY27, while revenue declined 7% from ₹455 Cr.

Including other income of ₹27 Cr, Ola Electric’s total income stood at ₹448 Cr, down 41% YoY from ₹756 Cr. Total expenses declined 28% YoY to ₹639 Cr from ₹893 Cr, although they rose 3% QoQ.

Ola Electric’s operating EBITDA loss increased 7% YoY to ₹218 Cr. Gross margin stood at 29.9%, against 30.5% in Q1 FY27 and 30.9% in the year-ago quarter. Ola Electric attributed the sequential moderation largely to higher commodity costs, partly offset by price increases.

The automotive business contributed ₹420 Cr to revenue, while the cell business generated ₹3 Cr. Inter-segment revenue, representing cells used in Ola’s own vehicles, stood at ₹2 Cr. 

The automotive business reported an operating EBITDA loss of ₹120 Cr, 2.6 times the loss in the year-ago quarter. The cell business, meanwhile, narrowed its operating EBITDA loss by 36% YoY to ₹32 Cr.

Against this backdrop, Ola Electric is attempting to reset its distribution and cost structure, while ramping up in-house cell manufacturing. The company’s immediate focus is on improving vehicle availability, reducing operating expenses and easing working capital requirements.

Ola Electric Shifts To Dealer-Led Distribution Model

A key part of this reset is Ola Electric’s transition from its erstwhile touted D2C distribution model to a more streamlined dealer-led network.

It had announced this shift earlier in Q2 (in August) and subsequently opened dealer stores on September 4. As of November 8, it had onboarded 255 dealer partners and established more than 300 stores. It now has set a target of operating 450 stores by December and 700 by March 2027.

Ola Electric stopped accepting orders through its D2C stores from November 1. Most company-owned stores are expected to close by December, with all new vehicle production routed to the dealer network.

The transition is expected to change the company’s cost structure. Dealers purchase vehicles from Ola Electric and maintain inventory at their own outlets, reducing the company’s need to manage a self-owned retail network as well as finance the inventory held at its stores.

As a result, the EV maker expects operating expenses to come down by ₹50 Cr. In its shareholder letter, it said operating expenses stood at ₹369 Cr in Q2 FY27, against ₹390 Cr in Q1, excluding a one-time non-cash reversal of ₹57 Cr in the June quarter.

However, the transition could weigh on gross margins in the near term. This pressure comes at the behest of the pay it dolls out as commissions to its dealers. The cost structure here is yet to be revealed.

Ola Electric expects the dealer commission structure to moderate over the next two to three quarters as the network stabilises. It expects the shift to start improving operating margins from Q3 FY27 onwards.

“Gross margins will come down a bit, but operating margins will meaningfully improve,” founder and Chairman Bhavish Aggarwal said during the earnings call.

The company said dealer sell-through was improving, with channel inventory at around 15 days. It also reported that dealers had begun placing repeat orders, indicating improving movement through the new distribution network.

Supply Chain: The Next Growth Constraint?

In its shareholder letter, Ola Electric said demand was no longer its primary constraint. It pointed instead to the pace at which its supply chain could scale production to meet demand.

“We reset our business and rebuilt it on a more sustainable model, which we are now growing. The main headline of Q2 FY27 is that demand is no longer our constraint; supply is. The constraint is not our manufacturing capacity but our supply chain’s ramp-up, which we are scaling rapidly,” it noted.

Production has remained broadly flat for several months but has started increasing month-on-month. Ola Electric expects to produce around 25,000 vehicles in December.

Aggarwal also highlighted the company’s cost advantage, claiming that its bill of materials (BOM) costs are 15-20% lower than those of competitors, despite its vehicles offering “higher functionality, battery capacity and better range.”

He attributed this advantage to vertical integration, in-house engineering and a more integrated component architecture, which reduces the number of components and dependence on external suppliers.

The company expects further cost savings from integrating its in-house lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells and Gen 4 platform into its vehicles from Q4 FY27 onwards.

Cash Flows, Debt And Working Capital Remain Key Priorities

Ola Electric continues to operate with negative cash flows. Its consolidated operating cash flow stood at negative ₹188 Cr, while free cash flow was negative ₹371 Cr during the quarter.

However, Aggarwal believes that operating cash flows were stabilising and improving sequentially. He attributed much of the difference between operating and free cash flow to capital expenditure at the Gigafactory.

The company said that it has strengthened its balance sheet through the recent qualified institutional placement (QIP) and rights issue over the past few months. The company raised ₹780 Cr via its QIP in June and another ₹1,000 Cr via a rights issue that culminated last week. 

Total borrowings declined to ₹1,819 Cr in September 2026 from ₹3,132 Cr in December 2024. Auto borrowings fell more sharply to ₹337 Cr from ₹2,422 Cr during the same period.

“With low auto debt, a healthy gross margin and cost structure, and a much improved working capital cycle under the dealer model, we expect auto to generate free cash flow in the near term,” the company said.

Further, the dealer-led model can also improve working capital because dealers pay for vehicles when placing orders and hold inventory at their own stores. This reduces the amount of working capital Ola Electric needs to deploy across its distribution network.

The company also expects changes to the GST refund mechanism, effective November 1, 2026, to ease working capital requirements. Under the revised framework, refunds under the inverted duty structure will cover GST paid on services in addition to raw materials. A provision for 90% auto-approval of eligible refunds is also expected to reduce the refund cycle from three to four months to one to two months.

Aggarwal said Ola Electric had already started reducing its GST receivables through internal operational improvements over the preceding two quarters. Of the roughly ₹1,000 Cr in GST receivables discussed during the earnings call, management estimated that 30-40% was linked to the inverted duty structure. The remaining amount would largely be adjusted against future business and should not be treated as immediately realisable cash.

Ola Electric Ramps Up Cell Production At Gigafactory

Beyond its automotive business, Ola Electric is looking to improve the economics of its cell manufacturing operations, which it sees as a key growth engine.

The company claims to have achieved the scheduled commercial operation date (SCOD) for its 6 GWh cell manufacturing capacity ahead of schedule. It is now focused on improving production yields and scaling output at the Gigafactory.

NMC cell yields were already in the mid-70% range, and the company expects them to reach 80-85% over the next few months before progressing towards 90%.

Aggarwal said the company had identified specific machines and quality parameters that needed attention to improve yields.

“We know exactly which machine we have to fix. We know exactly what kind of quality tests are helping us track and then how to improve it,” he said.

Ola Electric is also ramping up LFP cell production and expects yields to reach around 70% by the end of Q4 FY27. Integration of its in-house LFP cells into vehicles is expected towards the end of Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28.

The company expects its automotive cell mix to comprise around 30% NMC (nickel manganese cobalt) and 70% LFP cells. It estimates that its automotive business could consume 2-3 GWh of cells in FY28, equivalent to approximately 4-5 Lakh vehicles, assuming an average battery pack capacity of 5 kWh.

The economics of in-house cell manufacturing will depend heavily on improving yields. Ola Electric said its cells could achieve cost parity with externally sourced cells at around 70% yield. At 85% yield, it expects savings of 10-15% at the cell gross margin level.

Aggarwal also indicated that in-house manufacturing could provide a cost advantage of around 20% once production reaches the required scale.

The company plans to stabilise its existing 6 GWh capacity before expanding it to 20 GWh. The facility has already been designed to accommodate the larger capacity, which is expected to reduce incremental investment requirements. At 20 GWh, Ola Electric expects capital expenditure per GWh to fall below ₹400 Cr.

It is also looking to supply cells to other original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and tap demand from the energy storage market. The company plans to launch its Shakti Gen 2 product in Q4 FY27 and scale up the business in FY28.

With this, it seems that the next phase of Ola Electric’s turnaround will therefore depend on whether it can translate its manufacturing investments into higher vehicle output, improve cell yields and generate better operating cash flows, while the dealer-led model brings down the cost of selling and distributing its vehicles.

Shares of Ola electric ended today’s trading session 3.7% higher at ₹35.73 apiece on the BSE.

item.title: CCPA Fines Ola ₹10 Lakh For Advance Tipping Prompts
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of ₹10 Lakh on ANI Technologies Pvt Ltd, parent of…
item.content:encoded:
The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of ₹10 Lakh on ANI Technologies Pvt Ltd, parent of ride-hailing platform Ola, for misleading customers into paying extra to improve their chances of getting a ride.

In an order dated November 10, the consumer watchdog said Ola’s advance tipping feature is an unfair trade practice and an unfair contract under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

The CCPA also directed Ola to stop the practice immediately, pay the penalty within 15 days of receiving the order and submit a compliance report within the same period.

The proceedings followed a complaint received against this issue where the app prompted users to pay extra to get bookings faster.

“Adding a tip might help increase the chances of getting a ride faster,” a message read.

Customers were initially offered preset amounts ranging from ₹10 to ₹40. These later increased to as much as ₹140, while customers could also enter custom amounts of up to ₹499.

Ola argued that the payment was voluntary and went directly to drivers. It said the feature encouraged drivers to accept rides that were less attractive to them, particularly those requiring longer distances to reach passengers. The company also said that tipping did not affect its ride allocation system or guarantee faster ride confirmation.

However, the CCPA found that Ola’s own data did not support its claims. Data for June 1-15, 2026, showed that in Delhi, drivers accepted 38% of ride requests with an add-on, compared with 62% of requests without one. In Bengaluru, the acceptance rates were 40% and 68%, respectively, while in Mumbai they stood at 39% and 68%.

The authority also noted that Ola changed the feature’s name from ‘tip’ to ‘add-on’ on May 22, 2025, but continued to show messages suggesting that additional payments could help customers get a ride faster. During a hearing in June 2026, Ola demonstrated that its app still displayed messages such as “Improve your chances of quicker ride confirmation!” alongside preset payment amounts. The CCPA said the change in wording did not alter how the feature worked.

The authority also examined Ola’s data for Delhi, Bengaluru and Mumbai for June 1-15, 2026. The platform received nearly 39.94 Lakh ride requests across the three cities, of which 3.93 Lakh, or around 9.8%, included an add-on. Drivers accepted 1.51 Lakh of these requests.

Based on the average add-on amounts reported by Ola, the CCPA estimated that customers paid around ₹56 Lakh over and above the disclosed fares for these accepted rides.

The share of customers opting for add-ons also increased between June 2025 and June 2026. In Delhi, it rose from 8.2% to 11.04%, while in Bengaluru it increased from 9.7% to 10.64%. In Mumbai, it went up from 7.9% to 8.37%.

The CCPA rejected Ola’s argument that only a small number of customers used the feature, noting that everyone booking a ride was shown the prompts while waiting for confirmation.

It also said the feature could particularly affect people booking rides from hospitals, railway stations, bus terminals and airports, where they may be in a hurry and more dependent on getting a ride quickly.

CCPA Flags Confirm Shaming Dark Pattern

The CCPA’s action comes after the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) directed ride-hailing aggregators, including Uber, Rapido and Ola, to remove tipping prompts displayed before or during a ride, citing violations of the Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines, 2025.

In a directive dated August 11, the ministry flagged prompts such as “Advance Tip”, “Choose an Add-on” and “Improve your chances of quicker ride confirmation”. It also objected to messages suggesting that tipping could increase the chances of a driver accepting a ride.

Under Clause 14.15 of the guidelines, passengers can tip drivers only after completing a ride. Aggregators cannot offer tipping options during booking, before a ride starts or while it is in progress. The guidelines also stipulate that the entire tip must go to the driver, without any commission charged by the aggregator, and that tipping options must not be misleading or manipulative and must comply with the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

The CCPA rejected Ola’s argument that the additional payment was merely a voluntary tip, observing that tipping ordinarily represents appreciation for services already rendered, whereas Ola solicited payments before drivers accepted bookings.

It also highlighted a contradiction in Ola’s arguments. If the add-on did not influence ride acceptance, the representation that it improved booking chances was misleading. If it did, customers who did not pay were placed at a relative disadvantage.

The authority classified the interface as confirm shaming, a dark pattern prohibited under the Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023. It noted that the prompts created apprehension among customers that declining to pay could result in delayed confirmation or no ride at all. The absence of an option to decline or close the prompt was also flagged.

The CCPA further rejected Ola’s contention that it did not derive any commercial benefit from the feature because the entire add-on amount went to drivers. It observed that the feature could improve the platform’s attractiveness to drivers and its ride fulfilment rates, thereby serving Ola’s commercial interests.

In September 2026, the CCPA had imposed a similar ₹10 Lakh penalty on ride-hailing platform Rapido over its advance tipping feature, citing misleading advertisements, unfair trade practices and dark patterns.

While determining Ola’s penalty, the authority considered the scale and duration of the practice, its impact on consumers and the company’s financial position. It noted that Ola operated across more than 200 cities in India and had over 40 Mn users.

The CCPA also noted that Ola reported standalone revenue from operations of around ₹1,060 Cr in FY25. It said the ₹10 Lakh penalty was less than 0.01% of the company’s revenue and was warranted to deter similar violations.

GoKwik’s Golden Handcuffs

GoKwik has added a contentious twist to its ESOP policy. Under the new rules, current and former employees could forfeit their unvested and vested-but-unexercised options if they join any of GoKwik’s nine rivals. Can the startup use ESOPs to restrict where its talent goes next?

A New Kind Of Restriction: GoKwik’s amended ESOP Plan 2021 names Razorpay, Shiprocket, CRED, Cashfree Payments, BiteSpeed, Snapmint, WebEngage, Shopflo and Pine Labs as restricted companies. Employees cannot join, advise and invest in them without risking the loss of outstanding options. Crucially, the restriction applies retroactively to previously issued grants and extends for two full years after an employee’s departure.

Employees In Limbo: For GoKwik employees with significant ESOP holdings, the new policy has created a difficult choice between career mobility and potential wealth loss. Many are weighing offers from larger or better-known companies against the risk of forfeiting ESOPS they have already earned the right to exercise.

The timing has added to concerns. GoKwik has seen several senior-level departures in the recent past, while the recent layoff, earlier this year, is further adding to the staff’s concerns.

A Legal Gray Area: Non-compete clauses are common in Indian employment agreements, but explicitly linking rivals to the forfeiture of vested options is unusual. Legal experts believe that GoKwik’s amendment could face legal scrutiny if it is used to penalise employees for joining a competitor. 

The issue also raises governance concerns. By converting earned equity into an aggressive retention tactic, startups risk eroding the trust that underpins employee wealth creation. So, will GoKwik stand by its restrictive ESOP policy or roll back the controversial clause? Let’s find out…

From The Editor’s Desk

New CEO At Unacademy

  • Barely two months after upGrad completed the acquisition of the edtech platform, Gaurav Munjal is now stepping down as the CEO of Unacademy. He will now transition to the role of executive chairman at the startup and will “help” with upGrad’s IPO.
  • Meanwhile, Unacademy’s chief business officer Akhilendra Kumar will take over as the chief executive of the recently-acquired edtech platform. 
  • The transition marks the end of Munjal’s tenure as the top executive of the once-high flying edtech platform. Unacademy raised billions of dollars at the peak of the pandemic, but ran into monetisation issues and ballooning losses as soon as schools reopened.

RentoMojo’s Mixed Q2

  • The recently-listed furniture rental company saw its profits tank 62.6% YoY to ₹18.2 Cr in Q2 FY27. This decline was largely due to a deferred tax expense of ₹6.2 Cr in Q2 FY27 and a deferred tax credit of ₹32.8 Cr in the year-ago quarter.
  • Meanwhile, operating revenue grew 52.8% YoY to ₹142.1 Cr in Q2 FY27, driven by growth in customer orders, live subscribers and rental inventory. Nevertheless, expenses continued to bite and rose 53.2% YoY to ₹119.8 Cr.
  • On the operational front, Rentomojo expanded its network to 96 stores at the end of September 2026. The platform’s live subscriber base also grew 43% YoY to 3.2 Lakh, while users ordered 3.8 Lakh gross items during the quarter under review, up 45% YoY.

Cult.fit’s Trademark Dispute

  • The Madras HC has directed the IPO-bound gym chain to file its response on a petition, which seeks the cancellation of the CULT trademark held by one of Cult.fit’s subsidiaries. The matter has been scheduled for next hearing on December 2.
  • The plea in the HC was filed by Deepak Poduval, who cofounded the CULT fitness business in 2015. He alleges that his signatures on a 2017 assignment deeds, which purportedly transferred the brand to Cult.fit, were forged. 
  • If the challenge succeeds, the case could affect Cult.fit’s right to use the trademark. Additionally, the gym chain could also face SEBI scrutiny for previously acknowledging that its DRHP did not correctly describe the ownership of the CULT trademarks. 

Govt Bans Black Mass Exports

  • The directorate general of foreign trade has issued directions to prohibit export of ‘black mass’, a mineral-rich product of recycled EV batteries. The order will be applicable immediately to all outbound shipments of the battery waste material. 
  • Obtained from shredding end-of-life lithium-ion batteries, black mass is rich in metals like lithium, cobalt and nickel. These minerals can be recovered from the black mass and reused in new batteries, which could save costs and reduce foreign dependence.
  • While the restriction could retain critical raw materials within domestic borders, India still has limited capacity for black mass extraction and refining. As such, capabilities will have to be built up to capture the full economic value of black mass. 

Dull Diwali For Retailers

  • Weak consumer demand and rising prices weighed heavily on the recently-concluded Diwali festive season. According to AIMRA, mobile phone retailers saw sales volumes decline by 18-20% over the four-day period between November 6 and November 9. 
  • However, overall sales value remained broadly in line with last year’s festive season on the back of higher average selling prices. Nevertheless, AIMRA noted that the contraction in volumes squeezed margins and store profitability across retail channels.
  • The sub-₹20,000 segment was particularly impacted by a shortage of fresh, competitive 5G models from leading brands. On top of this, financing emerged as another constraint during the festive season as only 60-70% of the loan applications were approved.

Inc42 Markets

Inc42 Startup Spotlight

Can Qucev Break Diesel’s Grip On The Indian Freight?

India’s EV revolution is gathering pace, but heavy-duty trucks remain difficult to electrify because of heavy payloads, long duty cycles and patchy charging infrastructure. Qucev is trying to fix this gap with its indigenously designed and manufactured electric commercial vehicles.

Electrifying India’s Logistics: Founded in 2022, Qucev sells delivery and refrigerated vans, heavy-duty trucks, electric tractors, and electric concrete mixers. The startup caters to sectors including logistics, manufacturing, construction and cold-chain operations. Besides, it also offers charging support, financing partnerships, fleet tracking and after-sales services. 

The High-Mileage Ride: The Hyderabad-based startup operates two manufacturing facilities and operates a service network that spans 17 cities. Qucev claims that its vehicles, which have clocked over 1.3 Mn kms so far, cater to more than 20 enterprise customers, including DHL, Blue Dart, Mondelez and Godrej. 

The Road Ahead: Backed by Singularity AMC, the startup now plans to scale manufacturing and develop new products. But the road ahead may not be easy. Competing against rivals like Tata Motors and Euler Motors, its next challenge will be proving that its purpose-built electric trucks can deliver dependable economics at scale. So, can Qucev make heavy-duty electrification India’s next EV success story?

item.title: Retail Smartphone Sales Tanked 20% In 2026 Diwali Season: AIMRA
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: Weak consumer demand and rising prices weighed heavily on the offline smartphone market in the recently-concluded Diwali festive season.  According…
item.content:encoded:
Weak consumer demand and rising prices weighed heavily on the offline smartphone market in the recently-concluded Diwali festive season. 

According to industry body All India Mobile Retailers Association (AIMRA), mobile phone retailers saw sales volumes decline by 18-20% over the four-day period between Dhanteras (November 6) and the day after Diwali (November 9). 

However, overall sales value remained broadly in line with last year’s festive season on the back of higher average selling prices.

Nevertheless, AIMRA noted that the “steeper contraction” in volumes squeezed margins and store profitability across mainline retail channels.

The industry body also said that offline smartphone sales volumes in the seven days preceding Dhanteras plunged nearly 40% as consumers delayed purchases in anticipation of festive offers. However, the demand picked up as customer footfall grew during the four-day period.

Giving a breakdown of the demand data, the report noted that urban consumers showed muted interest in upgrading devices, while Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets recorded stronger momentum – especially particularly in the mid-segment. 

Most purchases were concentrated in the ₹30,000-60,000 price band after offers, while the premium segment also saw healthy demand, as per the report.

The sub-₹20,000 segment was particularly impacted by a shortage of fresh, competitive 5G models from leading brands. As a result, some value-conscious buyers shifted to brands such as HMD, Lava, Ai+, Tecno and itel, while others opted for pre-owned and refurbished devices to access higher specifications at lower prices. 

AIMRA also said that financing emerged as another constraint during the festive season. The industry body claimed that only 60-70% of logged loan applications were approved, leaving a significant share of prospective buyers unable to complete purchases due to tighter underwriting and CIBIL-related rejections. 

Performance also varied sharply across brands. Apple and Google Pixel saw strong demand, as did Xiaomi, which benefited from competitive pricing. Meanwhile, Vivo, OPPO and Samsung also maintained healthy sales by value but saw weaker unit volumes. 

Realme saw volumes plunge by over 50% across regions, as per AIMRA. “This drop was triggered by uncompetitive pricing compared to Xiaomi, Samsung, and Vivo, zero new festive launches, and unlucrative consumer schemes. Market acceptance above ₹40,000 remains weak, dimming its near-term outlook,” said the industry body. 

Why Are Smartphones Becoming Pricey?

Largely to blame for the subdued festive season was price hikes by smartphone companies and rising commodity prices. This comes as the ongoing AI boom has dried up the supply of many critical components for entry-level and budget smartphone makers, which operate on razor-thin profit margins.

This is because memory chips makers are actively prioritising the demand from data centres and AI infrastructure providers, where margins are higher. 

As a result, the per-device memory cost has already increased to $60-65, a 3X jump from around $20 in 2025, per a recent Jefferies report. As a result, the brokerage firm expects the prices of low-end smartphones to increase nearly 30%. 

Overall, consulting giant Deloitte expects the memory shortage to last until as late as 2030. 

To tide over this, smartphone makers have resorted to price hikes to pass on the higher component costs to consumers. Retail prices of existing smartphones have increased by as much 21% in India on an average, as per Counterpoint Research. 

The memory crisis has also particularly impacted the budget segment of the market, where manufacturers have limited room to absorb cost increases without sacrificing margins. This explains why India, a relatively price-sensitive market, has been heavily impacted. 

The trend is expected to hold going forward as well. Xiaomi has already signalled price increases of up to ₹4,000 across product categories, while other smartphone makers are preparing hikes of up to 15%. 

With festive footfall already moderating, the AIMRA expects sales volumes at mainline brick-and-mortar stores to contract by as much as 50% over the next three months.

item.title: After A Decade-Long Stint, Gaurav Munjal To Step Down As Unacademy CEO
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: Barely two months after rival upGrad acquired Unacademy, cofounder Gaurav Munjal is now stepping down as the chief executive officer…
item.content:encoded:
Barely two months after rival upGrad acquired Unacademy, cofounder Gaurav Munjal is now stepping down as the chief executive officer (CEO) of the test prep platform. 

In a post on LinkedIn, Munjal said that he will now transition to the role of executive chairman at the startup. Unacademy cofounder also added that he will be “fully involved” in the day-to-day operations of the recently-acquired startup and will “help” with upGrad’s initial public offering (IPO).

Meanwhile, Unacademy chief business officer (CBO) Akhilendra Kumar will take over as the chief executive of the recently-acquired edtech platform. 

Unacademy chief business officer Kumar was vice president of business until 2025 before taking over the role as CBO. Prior to that, he has worked with OYO under various leadership roles for nearly four years. He has also been previously associated with Exide Industries.

“I’m moving from CEO to executive chairman of Unacademy, and Akhilendra Kumar will take over as CEO. To be clear, I’m not going anywhere. I’ll stay fully involved in operations every day, work alongside Akhilendra and help with the upGrad IPO. Akhilendra is one of the sharpest operators I know, and I’m proud to have him lead us into this next chapter…,” Munjal said in the post.

With Munjal’s exit, all cofounders, including Roman Saini, Hemesh Singh and Sumit Jain, have now left the startup. In May this year, Inc42 exclusively reported that Jain had stepped down from the edtech startup as chief executive, leaving Munjal to take over the reins of the platform.

While there appears no clarity on Munjal’s next course of action, his departure comes a month after reports first surfaced that Munjal, along with fellow Unacademy cofounder Saini, was looking to raise a ₹700 Cr venture capital fund to back AI and deeptech startups.

Called Longshot Capital, the category II AIF has reportedly already secured commitments of around ₹250-300 Cr and is targeting its first close in January 2027. 

That said, the transition marks the end of Munjal’s decade-long tenure as the chief executive at the edtech platform. He founded Unacademy in 2015 as a YouTube channel and scaled the edtech platform to unicorn valuation at the height of the pandemic in 2020.

However, things started to unravel after the re-opening of offline educational institutions. This hit demand for online learning, prompting Unacademy to undertake multiple rounds of layoffs, reduce its cash burn, and shut or scale down several verticals.

Unacademy subsequently held acquisition discussions with multiple companies including Allen Career Institute, K-12 Techno Services, and upGrad. Its earlier talks with upGrad fell through over valuation differences before the two companies revived negotiations and signed a term sheet in March this year. upGrad finally completed the acquisition in September for just over $200 Mn.

item.title: Centre Bans Export of Lithium-Ion Battery’s ‘Black Mass’
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: In a major regulatory shift for India’s EV supply chain ecosystem, the Centre has issued directions to prohibit export of…
item.content:encoded:
In a major regulatory shift for India’s EV supply chain ecosystem, the Centre has issued directions to prohibit export of ‘black mass’, a mineral-rich product of recycled EV batteries. 

The directorate general of foreign trade (DGFT), under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, notified the amendment yesterday. It is immediately applicable to all outbound shipments of the battery waste material. 

“The export policy of waste and scrap of primary cells, primary batteries and electric accumulators; spent primary cells, spent primary batteries and spent electric accumulators – Unsorted and not containing lead, cadmium or mercury (Lithium-lon Battery Black Mass) under ITC (HS) Code 85491400 is amended from ‘Free’ to ‘Prohibited’ with immediate effect, until further orders,” the directorate said in a circular. 

For context, black mass is a powder obtained from shredding end-of-life lithium ion batteries that is rich in valuable metals like lithium, cobalt, and nickel. These metals can be recovered from the black mass and reused in new batteries, which saves costs compared to mining fresh reserves. 

As India is dependent on imports for these raw materials, black mass has strategic value by enabling these metals to be sourced locally. 

The new export policy ties into the centre’s strategic push to reduce India’s dependence on imports of critical minerals. In September 2025, the government approved incentives worth ₹1,500 Cr to develop domestic capacity for recycling critical minerals. 

It followed up on the move earlier this week with the Capex Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing, which committed an outlay of ₹2,814 Cr to set up two plants each for lithium and nickel processing. 

According to the Observer Research Foundation, India can recycle over 60,000 tonnes of batteries per year, which can generate around 30,000 tonnes of black mass. However, due to limited processing capacity, the black mass typically gets exported to foreign markets. 

Hence, this new restriction could retain critical raw materials within domestic borders. That said, India’s black mass extraction and refining capabilities still need to be built up in order to ensure that the full economic value can be captured. 

India’s battery recycling market reached $603.9 Mn in 2025 and is projected to reach $1.3 Bn by 2034, growing at a CAGR of 8.65%. As the battery manufacturing ecosystem scales, ensuring that strategic materials can be processed within domestic borders will be critical to building a more resilient supply chain.

item.title: [Update] Greenjoules Closes Series B Round At ₹150 Cr
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Update | November 11, 17:18 IST Months after Inc42 exclusively reported on Greenjoules’s fundraise, the cleantech startup announced the closure…
item.content:encoded:
Update | November 11, 17:18 IST

Months after Inc42 exclusively reported on Greenjoules’s fundraise, the cleantech startup announced the closure of its Series B round at ₹150 Cr ($16 Mn). The round was co-led by Amazon’s Smbhav Venture Fund and Climate Pledge Fund, with participation from Rainmatter and Singularity’s Strategic Autonomy Fund.

The startup said that the fresh funds will support its new plant at Pune’s Khed City with the capacity to produce 2 Lakh litres of biocrude a day from agricultural waste. The facility will be developed in phases from 2027, which is expected to be the largest of its kind in India.

Additionally, Greenjoules also secured a ₹100 Cr debt from Technology Development Board (TDB), under the Government of India’s Department of Science and Technology.

“Greenjoules was built without a map; every step forward meant first inventing the path. We took two things that looked irreconcilable — low-energy-density agricultural waste and specification-grade fuel — and spent more than six years proving they were one and the same. With the concept proven and partners such as TDB and our Series B investors behind us, we are ready to make a deep impact on the global energy market, and to carry that pioneering spirit into sustainable aviation fuel,green hydrogen and sustainable materials.” said Shweta Viraraghavan, cofounder and chief technology officer, Greenjoules.

Original | August 21, 18:58 IST

Pune-based green energy startup Greenjoules has raised about ₹62 Cr ($6.5 Mn) in what appears to be an ongoing Series B funding round. 

While Amazon’s investment arm, Amazon.com NV Investment Holdings, is leading the funding round, Singularity AMC’s Singularity Strategic Autonomy Fund also participated in the round.

As per MCA filings accessed by Inc42, the startup’s board allotted 40,338 Series B1 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at ₹11,155.5 apiece for ₹45 Cr to Amazon.com NV Investment Holdings LLC.

Separately, it also allotted 15,238 Series B1 CCPS to a sum of about ₹17 Cr to Singularity Strategic Autonomy Fund. 

Greenjoules declined to comment on Inc42’s queries regarding the total size of the round. 

Founded in 2018 by S Viraraghavan, V Radhika, VS Shridhar and R Sethunath, Greenjoules converts farm residues into renewable fuels that can be used in existing diesel engines and industrial equipment, effectively substituting crude oil with agricultural waste.

The startup is developing green fuels that can cater to sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), green hydrogen and biomethane areas. 

Prior to the ongoing round, the climatetech startup raised $4.5 Mn in a combination of equity and debt from Blue Ashva Capital in 2021, to set up commercial scale waste to energy plants and invest into new R&D initiatives.

The investor interest in the eight-year old startup aligns with India’s broader push to scale renewable fuel sources in a bid to attain the country’s net zero goals.

India aims to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by the year 2070. Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced this target during the COP26 climate summit in Glasgow, backed by a climate plan known as the “Panchamrita”.

The country’s long-term low-carbon development strategy rests on seven key transitions to low-carbon development pathways. These include low-carbon development of electricity systems, enhancing forest and vegetation cover consistent with socioeconomic, development of CO2 removal and related engineering solutions, among others.

Amid this push, India’s cleantech market is projected to become a $152.5 Bn market by 2030, creating a suitable market opportunity for new and emerging players as well as more established industrial players to leverage the opportunity.
