item.title: Rentomojo Q2 Revenue Jumps 53% YoY To ₹142 Cr, Net Profit Slumps 63%
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: Recently listed furniture rental company Rentomojo reported a 62.6% year-on-year (YoY) decline in its profit after tax to ₹18.2 Cr…
item.content:encoded:
Recently listed furniture rental company Rentomojo reported a 62.6% year-on-year (YoY) decline in its profit after tax to ₹18.2 Cr in the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (Q2 FY27) from ₹48.6 Cr in the year-ago quarter. 

The decline was largely due to a deferred tax credit of ₹32.8 Cr recognised in the year-ago quarter, compared with a deferred tax expense of ₹6.2 Cr in Q2 FY27. 

On a sequential basis, the company’s net consolidated profit zoomed 133% from ₹7.8 Cr in the previous quarter. 

Meanwhile, operating revenue grew 52.8% YoY and 12% QoQ to ₹142.1 Cr in the quarter under review, driven by growth in customer orders, live subscribers and rental inventory. Including other income of ₹1.7 Cr, total income for the quarter stood at ₹143.8 Cr.

Total expenses increased 53.2% YoY to ₹119.8 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹78.2 Cr in the year-ago period. Employee benefit expenses rose 38.3% to ₹19.5 Cr, while finance costs increased 46.7% to ₹9 Cr.

The company said its normalised profit after tax, excluding exceptional items and deferred tax adjustments, increased 52.2% YoY to ₹24 Cr from ₹15.8 Cr in Q2 FY26. Normalised EBITDA also grew 52.7% to ₹58.8 Cr from ₹38.5 Cr a year earlier.

Subscriber Additions, Higher Utilisation Drive Growth

Rentomojo expanded its omnichannel network to 96 experience stores across 14 cities by the end of September, compared with 67 stores a year earlier. 

Customers ordered 3.8 Lakh gross items during the quarter, up 45% higher than last year’s quarter. Besides, the company’s live subscriber base grew 42.5% to approximately 3.2 Lakh, while live item inventory increased 44% to 10.5 Lakh.

Average occupancy grew by 61 basis points to 85.9% while average revenue per item (ARPI) increased 4.6% YoY to ₹1,650.

The company also reported higher asset utilisation. Assets procured in the FY17 cycle  generated cumulative revenue equivalent to 5.3X its original value, with around 54% of the cohort continuing to generate revenue. The FY18 cohort had generated 4.71X its original value, with 59.2% of its items still generating revenue.

For context, higher utilisation of its rental assets allows the company to generate repeat revenue from its asset base. Purchase displaced, which measures the estimated retail value of consumer purchases replaced by customers choosing to rent furniture, grew 61% YoY and 8% QoQ to ₹446.9 Cr.

This was the company’s second quarterly results following its public market debut in September after it raised ₹1,255.6 Cr from an initial public offering.  

The company said it had utilised ₹90 Cr, or 63.7%, of the ₹141.4 Cr net proceeds allocated to the IPO’s stated objectives as of September 30. This included the complete utilisation of ₹70 Cr earmarked for debt repayment, ₹8.1 Cr towards warehouse and experience store lease rentals, and ₹11.9 Cr for general corporate purposes.

Commenting on the performance, founder, chairperson, managing director and CEO Geetansh Bamania said the company would continue focusing on subscriber growth, better asset utilisation and technology while maintaining profitability, cash generation and returns on capital.

Shares of Rentomojo ended today’s trading session 3.30% higher at ₹610.9 apiece on the BSE.

item.title: IPO-Bound Cult.fit Faces Fresh Legal Challenge Over CULT Trademark
item.dc:creator: Debarghya Sil
item.description: In a fresh legal challenge ahead of Cult.fit’s proposed public listing, the Madras High Court (HC) has issued a notice…
item.content:encoded:
In a fresh legal challenge ahead of Cult.fit’s proposed public listing, the Madras High Court (HC) has issued a notice on a petition seeking cancellation of the CULT trademark registration held by one of the company’s subsidiaries.

The rectification petition was filed by Deepak Poduval, who cofounded the CULT fitness business in Bengaluru in 2015. He has approached the court seeking cancellation of the trademark registration held by Cultfit Healthcare Pvt Ltd, a subsidiary of Cult.fit, alleging that the documents used to establish ownership of the brand were forged.

The court issued notice in the matter (OP(TM) No. 51 of 2026) on October 12, 2026. During a hearing on November 5, it adjourned the proceedings to December 2, allowing Cultfit Healthcare to file its response.

Separately, Poduval has approached the Commercial Court in Bengaluru, seeking to have the 2017 deeds that purportedly transferred the CULT brand declared void. He has alleged that the signatures on these documents were forged. The matter is scheduled for its next hearing on November 16.

How The CULT Trademark Dispute Began

The dispute over the CULT trademark dates back to 2015, when Poduval first applied for the ‘CULT – The Workout Station’ trademark in August that year.

Cultfit Healthcare filed a separate trademark application in November 2016, claiming usage of the brand from May 1, 2015 — the same first-use date mentioned in Poduval’s application.

When the Trademark Registry raised objections citing Poduval’s earlier application, Cultfit Healthcare did not produce the alleged assignment deeds. Instead, it claimed to be the prior user and owner of the trademark in its own right.

Poduval has since challenged the validity of the 2017 assignment deeds that purportedly transferred the brand to Cultfit Healthcare. He alleges that his signatures on the documents were forged and has cited a privately commissioned forensic examination that, according to him, supports his allegations.

Cult.fit, however, has denied the allegations, maintaining that Poduval signed the assignment deeds.

In a statement, Poduval said the dispute concerns the ownership of a brand that has become central to a company preparing to go public. He added that investors deserve transparency about how Cult.fit acquired the trademark.

Trademark Dispute Part Of Larger Cofounder Row

The trademark challenge is part of a broader legal battle between CULT’s cofounders, Deepak Poduval and Rishabh Telang, over the transfer of the fitness business’s assets and intellectual property to the Mukesh Bansal-led startup.

In August 2026, Poduval filed an FIR against Telang at Bengaluru’s Bellandur Police Station, alleging forgery, cheating and criminal conspiracy in connection with the 2016 transfer of certain assets and intellectual property from Cult Fitness Pvt Ltd to Cultfit Healthcare Pvt Ltd.

Poduval alleged that Telang forged his signatures on multiple documents used to wind up Cult Fitness, including board resolutions, shareholder consent documents and statutory filings. He also claimed that 50% of his shareholding in the company was extinguished without any consideration.

Telang denied the allegations, maintaining that Poduval was involved in the transactions and the subsequent winding up of Cult Fitness. He further claimed that Poduval had received consideration for the transfer.

Cult.fit also maintained that the transaction was carried out under appropriate contractual arrangements and that the consideration was duly paid and acknowledged by Poduval. The company added that neither it nor its subsidiary was an accused in the FIR.

Following the FIR, Telang moved the Karnataka High Court seeking to quash the case. The court sought responses from Poduval and the state but did not stay the investigation.

The latest petition before the Madras HC takes the dispute beyond the alleged transfer of assets, directly challenging the legal ownership of the CULT trademark held by Cultfit Healthcare.

What The Dispute Means For Cult.fit’s IPO

The trademark challenge also raises questions about how Cult.fit has disclosed the ownership of the CULT brand in its draft IPO prospectus.

In a written response dated October 14 to a complaint filed by Poduval with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), Cult.fit acknowledged that its draft prospectus did not correctly describe the ownership of the CULT trademarks.

The company clarified that the trademarks are registered in the name of Cultfit Healthcare Pvt Ltd and not Cult.fit Ltd. It also undertook to correct the disclosure in its final prospectus.

With the subsidiary’s trademark registration now under challenge before the Madras HC, the dispute could become a point of scrutiny for prospective investors.

Poduval has also questioned the company’s treatment of the CULT acquisition in its IPO disclosures. According to his complaint, Cult.fit has described the acquisition as ‘not material’.

While the draft prospectus does not name the acquisition, the company has made the deeds relating to Fitness First, another brand acquired by the group, available for investor inspection. However, the corresponding deeds for CULT have not been made available, Poduval alleged.

The challenge is significant given the extent to which Cult.fit uses the CULT brand across its operations. According to its draft IPO prospectus, hundreds of fitness centres operate under the brand. It also extends to Cult Neo gyms and the company’s Cultgear products business.

If the trademark challenge succeeds, it could potentially affect the group’s rights to use, license or transfer the brand, raising questions about the implications for its operations and brand ownership.

Cult.fit has filed its draft IPO papers for a proposed public issue. The company plans to raise up to ₹950 Cr through a fresh issue of shares, while existing investors are looking to offload up to 17.86 Cr shares through an offer for sale (OFS). The total IPO size is expected to be around ₹4,000 Cr.

item.title: Fintech SaaS Company Veefin Migrates To NSE, BSE Mainboard
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht

item.content:encoded:
Update| Nov 11, 18:43 IST

Shares of Veefin ended today’s trading session 2% higher at ₹248.70 apiece on the BSE, while they closed 2.1% higher at ₹249 apiece on the NSE.

Original| Nov 11, 13:38 IST

BSE SME listed Veefin Solutions has migrated to the main board of the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the BSE, more than three years after its SME IPO. Veefin’s shares opened for trade on the BSE mainboard at ₹249.75 (2.5% higher than previous close) and at ₹250.84 on the NSE.

Veefin’s market capitalisation as of 13:20 IST stood at ₹633.76 Cr ($67.61 Mn). Shares of Veefin were trading 1.2% higher at ₹249 apiece on the BSE and 1.2% higher at ₹246.65 apiece on the NSE around 13:30 IST.

Veefin listed on the BSE SME platform in July 2023 at ₹86.05, a near 5% premium from its IPO price. The company’s ₹46.73 Cr IPO comprised about 57 Lakh shares, with equal parts of fresh issue and offer for sale shares. 

Its mainboard debut comes on the heels of the company solidifying its financial position over the recent quarter. Its operating revenue for the first half of the ongoing fiscal year (H1 FY27) doubled to ₹238.8 Cr while its consolidated net profit zoomed 127% YoY to ₹24.9 Cr.

Veefin reported a 127% year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated net profit to ₹24.9 Cr in H1 FY27 from ₹11 Cr in the corresponding period last year. Net profit was also up 9% from ₹22.8 Cr in H2 FY26.

In Q2 FY27, Veefin’s net profit rose 61% sequentially to ₹15.3 Cr from ₹9.5 Cr in the preceding quarter. Operating revenue increased 9% sequentially to ₹124.7 Cr from ₹114.2 Cr, while total income stood at ₹125.7 Cr.

The company also reported a deal pipeline of around ₹920 Cr alongside its half-year results. Around 84% of the pipeline comprises opportunities from banks and financial institutions outside India, with Southeast Asia emerging as a key market.

The mainboard listing is expected to widen access to Veefin’s shares among retail and institutional investors. Unlike the fixed trading lots on the SME platform, the main boards allow investors to buy and sell shares individually.

Veefin Bets On AI Employees

In a statement, the fintech SaaS company said that it will now look at expanding beyond fintech with an AI platform that enables businesses to deploy digital employees for defined roles. Alongside the listing, the company announced a rebranding from veefin.com to veefin.ai, reflecting the growing role of AI in its products and growth strategy.

Its next growth opportunity is through the Veefin AI Operating System (AIOS), a platform designed to help businesses create, deploy and supervise AI employees for defined roles.

Veefin has developed more than 1,000 reusable AI skills and has started deploying AIOS internally across three functions: customer implementation, customer support and software testing. The company is using these deployments to improve productivity and build experience before offering the platform to customers.

The company sees an opportunity to cross-sell the platform to its current customers and reach enterprises beyond the financial services sector.

“We listed on the SME platform three years ago as a supply chain finance technology company. We come to the main boards as a multi-product company whose revenue has more than doubled in the past year, and with many more investors able to take part in what we build next,” Gautam Udani, vice chairperson, cofounder and COO of Veefin Group, said.

Founded in 2020 by Udani and Raja Debnath, Mumbai-based Veefin develops lending, supply chain finance and transaction banking software for banks, NBFCs, fintech companies and enterprises.

The company began with supply chain finance and has since expanded into trade finance, cash and liquidity management, loan origination, loan management, collections, and corporate and retail digital banking. Its customers use its technology through complete applications, platforms or individual components integrated into their own systems.

Veefin has also expanded through acquisitions and strategic investments, including stakes in digital marketing firm White Rivers Media, generative AI startup Walnut AI and lending enablement platform EpikInDiFi.

The mainboard transition follows a similar move by E2E Networks, which made its BSE mainboard debut in June after being listed on the NSE since 2018. E2E took the direct listing route to list its shares on the BSE.

item.title: ED Attaches ₹14 Cr Assets In HashPe Crypto Ponzi Fraud Case
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: The Enforcement Directorate (ED), Chennai, has provisionally attached movable and immovable assets worth approximately ₹14.2 Cr in connection with an…
item.content:encoded:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED), Chennai, has provisionally attached movable and immovable assets worth approximately ₹14.2 Cr in connection with an alleged cryptocurrency investment fraud operated by Pan India Cryptocurrency, HashPe.

The attachment was made on October 30, 2026, under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002. The ED has also filed a prosecution complaint before the Special Court (PMLA), Puducherry.

According to the ED, Hashpay allegedly operated a fraudulent cryptocurrency-based ponzi investment scheme that lured investors with promises of daily returns of 1%, returns of up to 3X the invested amount, referral commissions and rewards such as luxury cars and foreign trips.

The agency said the attached assets include immovable properties in Tamil Nadu, Haryana and New Delhi, a BMW car and funds deposited in bank accounts.

The investigation was initiated based on an FIR registered by the Cyber Crime Police Station, Puducherry, under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, and the Information Technology Act, 2000.

How The Ponzi Scheme Worked

ED’s investigation found that HashPe operated through a website, hashpe.io, and a multi-level marketing network. Its promoters allegedly used cash payments, bank transfers and cryptocurrency transactions to mobilise investments from the public.

The scheme reportedly used USDT (Tether), a stablecoin, and Bitcoin to facilitate transactions. However, the agency found that the purported trading activities were not backed by actual cryptocurrency trading.

Instead, money collected from new investors was allegedly used to repay earlier investors and pay commissions to agents. Withdrawals were eventually stopped and the platform was frozen, leaving investors with financial losses.

The ED further found that the promoters allegedly created fictitious cryptocurrency tokens, including TCX and HashPe, at an almost zero acquisition cost and assigned artificial values to them. The platform displayed profits to investors despite the absence of genuine cryptocurrency trading activity to generate the promised returns.

To attract investors, the promoters used celebrity endorsements, promotional events featuring luxury cars and gold, and foreign cruises to build credibility. They also established a multi-level marketing network, with agents designated as ‘Leaders’ receiving commissions for bringing in new investors. 

The ED said approximately ₹112.91 Cr was collected through the scheme, a portion of which was returned to investors. The remaining funds were transferred to bank accounts of ‘HIFY Circle’ and other related entities before being converted into cryptocurrency.

The proceeds were allegedly diverted towards personal expenses, loan repayments, hefty commissions and promotional activities, among other purposes.

The agency has identified approximately ₹49.54 Cr as proceeds of crime in the case.

The development comes after the ED conducted search operations at premises linked to HashPe, its promoters and associates on September 1. 

Following the searches, four individuals namely Imran Basha, Hitesh Kumar, Syed Usman alias Babu, and Dharmendra were arrested under Section 19 of the PMLA, 2002. All four accused are currently in judicial custody while the investigation is ongoing. 

The investigation revealed that Usman handled large cash investments and operated the HIFY Circle bank account, while Dhamodharan managed HashPe’s software, database and cryptocurrency operations, including its wallet functions. 

Heightened Crypto Crackdowns

Branches of ED across the country have stepped up the heat on suspected illegal cryptocurrency activities in recent months. On November 7, the ED in Bengaluru conducted searches at premises linked to crypto exchanges CoinDCX and Delta Exchange India (DEI) over alleged unauthorised cross-border transactions involving crypto derivatives and tokenised foreign stocks.

It had earlier conducted similar searches on October 29 at premises links to  crypto platforms Mudrex and Saber.money, as well as decentralised finance (DeFi) protocol Instadapp and its associated platform Fluid, over alleged unauthorised cross-border fund transfers worth more than ₹4,940 Cr.

Prior to this in June this year, the ED had also searched six premises linked to five platforms, namely Transak, Carret, Xpat, Onramp.money and Onmeta, over alleged unauthorised cross-border crypto transfers.

item.content:encoded:
Update | November 11, 12:15 IST

Kissht parent OnEMI Technology Solutions has completed its ₹832.20 Cr preferential issue, allotting 2.65 Cr equity shares to 34 investors at ₹314.1 apiece. Twenty four new investors picked up stake in the company, while 10 existing shareholders, including schemes from Alchemy, First Bridge, Groww and HDFC, increased their holdings.

The new investors include Axis Mutual Fund schemes, Ashoka WhiteOak funds, 360 ONE, Bandhan Small Cap Fund, Citigroup Global Markets Hong Kong, Unity Small Finance Bank and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT).

The shares received trading approval from BSE and NSE on November 8, following the board’s approval on October 23 and shareholders’ nod at an extraordinary general meeting on October 14.

The preferential issue will increase Kissht’s paid-up equity capital from ₹17.81 Cr to ₹20.46 Cr, with the newly allotted shares accounting for approximately 13% of its enlarged equity capital.

Original | September 18, 00:16 IST

Listed NBFC Kissht has secured board approval to raise up ₹832.2 Cr via a preferential issue of equity shares to 34 investors and entities. 

In a filing with the exchanges, the company said that its board has approved the issuance of 2.6 Cr fully paid-up equity shares to the investors at an issue price of ₹314.11 apiece. The NBFC did not disclose how it plans to utilise the fresh proceeds from the issue.

The allotment is still subject to regulatory and shareholder approval. The company has also convened an extraordinary general meeting of the shareholders to seek approval for the preferential issue.

“Funds raising by way of a preferential issue on a private placement basis of up to 2,64,93,882 fully paid-up equity shares of the company… for cash, at an issue price of ₹314.11 per share… for an amount aggregating to ₹832.19 Cr to identified investors (non-promoters), in accordance with the provisions of… applicable laws….,” read the filing.

Among the investing companies, Axis Flexi Cap Fund, Axis Multi Cap Fund and Axis Small Cap Fund together will receive 63.7 Lakh shares worth nearly ₹200 Cr. Massachusetts Institute of Technology, via two entities, will also receive 27.1 Lakh shares totalling ₹85 Cr.

Envision Capital will also get 12.7 Lakh shares valued at nearly ₹40 Cr, while PE firm First Bridge will lap up 12.1 Lakh shares for a sum of ₹20 Cr. 

Kissht will also allot 23.9 Lakh shares to three entities linked to Ashoka WhiteOak Capital for a consideration of nearly ₹75 Cr. Other investors that will receive allotment under the preferential issue include 360 One, Alchemy Capital, Groww, Bandhan Small Cap Fund, Unity Small Finance Bank, among others.

In terms of the other individual investors, Ameeta Rajendra Naik will receive 63,671 shares worth ₹2 Cr and Anil Shah will get 1.6 Lakh shares valued at nearly ₹5 Cr.

The latest fundraise comes barely four months after the NBFC made a strong debut on the exchanges, listing at a premium of 11.7% on the BSE compared to its issue price of ₹171. Its public issue comprised a fresh issue of shares worth ₹850 Cr and an OFS component totalling ₹76 Cr.

Founded in 2015 by Ranvir Singh and Krishnan Vishwanathan, Kissht is a lending tech platform that offers digital personal and business loans of up to ₹5 Lakh. It also offers health-related insurance products and secured loans through loans against property.

In July, it also received regulatory approval to begin distribution of mutual funds through its wholly-owned subsidiary Invincible Minds.

The NBFC claimed to have 45+ active lending and co-lending partners under its belt at the end of June 2026. It also operated 101 offline branches across eight states and union territories, and managed to more than double YoY its active customer base to 3.49 Mn in Q1 FY27. 

On the financial front, Kissht’s consolidated net profit zoomed 59% to ₹95.1 Cr in Q1 FY27 as against ₹59.7 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Meanwhile, operating revenue zoomed nearly 45% to ₹669.5 Cr during the quarter under review as against ₹463.1 Cr in Q1 FY26. 

Shares of the NBFC closed Thursday’s trading session 5.08% higher at ₹359.7 on the BSE.

item.title: AI, Financial Services, Better Connections: Kunal Shah Outlines Three Priorities For WhatsApp
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht

item.content:encoded:
Under its new global head Kunal Shah, WhatsApp is looking to expand beyond messaging. In a social media post, Shah said that the Meta-owned platform would focus on making services such as bill payments, financial transactions and international connectivity as seamless as sending a message.

Shah, who took charge of WhatsApp earlier this year, said the messaging platform would focus on three broad areas — making communication more expressive, simplifying everyday tasks and using AI to improve user experiences.

WhatsApp users could potentially complete tasks such as paying bills, borrowing money and staying connected while travelling without having to navigate multiple platforms or services.

“We’re working with financial services and telecom partners so that finishing something feels as easy as starting it,” he said.

Shah’s statement signals WhatsApp’s intent to deepen its push into financial services and commerce, building on its existing payments and business offerings. 

In India, the platform has been expanding its payments capabilities through WhatsApp Pay, although its adoption has remained limited compared with established UPI players.

It also outlined plans to integrate AI more deeply into the messaging experience, with the technology expected to help users find relevant information, complete tasks and keep track of bookings and appointments.

“The best technology saves you time, so you can get back to the connections that matter,” he said.

However, Shah did not specify which AI capabilities the company plans to introduce or whether these would involve more advanced agentic features. It currently offers AI-powered features through Meta AI, including assistance with queries and content generation.

WhatsApp’s Three Priorities

On the communication front, WhatsApp wants to make features such as voice notes, groups, stickers and video simpler and more expressive. Shah said users send more than 10 Bn voice messages and 4 Bn stickers on the platform every day, highlighting how communication habits continue to evolve.

It also wants to reduce the number of steps involved in completing everyday activities that originate in conversations. This could involve deeper integrations with financial services and telecom partners, although Shah did not disclose specific partnerships or timelines.

The third priority is the use of AI to make the platform more efficient by helping users retrieve information and manage everyday tasks.

However, Shah emphasised that these changes would not come at the cost of user privacy. He reiterated that personal messages and calls on WhatsApp would remain end-to-end encrypted.

“Whatever we build, WhatsApp must remain simple, reliable and private. These principles we’ve had for years aren’t changing,” he said.

Shah’s remarks come nearly five months after he moved from CRED to Meta to take over as the global head of WhatsApp.

In June 2026, Shah announced that he would step down from day-to-day operations at CRED to join Meta. CRED cofounder Miten Sampat took over as interim CEO, while Shah retained his personal shareholding in the fintech startup.

His appointment also marked a leadership transition at WhatsApp, with former head Will Cathcart moving to a new role within Meta.

Shah’s move came alongside Meta’s investment in CRED as part of the fintech startup’s ₹8,550 Cr Series H funding round, which valued the company at ₹43,239 Cr post-money.

At WhatsApp, Shah now faces the challenge of expanding the platform’s utility beyond communication while maintaining its simplicity and privacy standards.

India, WhatsApp’s largest market globally, has an estimated 535 Mn to 550 Mn monthly active users, with some industry databases putting the figure as high as 853.8 Mn. 

Globally, the platform has more than 3 Bn users. However, driving adoption of its payments, financial services and other offerings will remain a key challenge.
